source_text: Χρόνος δὲ οὗτος πάντων γέμει τῶν ἐναντιωτήτων, τοκετῶν, εἶτα θανάτων, βλαστήσεως φυτῶν, εἶτα ἀνατροπῆς· ἰάσεων καὶ ἀναιρέσεων, οἴκων τε εὐορθώσεως καὶ καταλύσεως, κλαυθμῶν καὶ γελώτων, κοπετῶν καὶ ὀρχημάτων. Νῦν μὲν συνάγει τις τὰ ἀπὸ γῆς, νῦν δὲ ἐξέβαλε· καὶ ποτὲ μὲν ἐπιμέμηνε γυναικί, ποτὲ δὲ αὐτὴν ἀποστυχεῖ. Καὶ νῦν μὲν ἐζήτησέ τις ὁτιοῦν, νῦν δὲ ἀπώλεσε· καὶ νῦν μὲν ἐφύλαξε, νῦν δὲ προήκατο· ἄλλοτε ἀπέκτεινεν, ἄλλοτε ἐφονεύθη· ἐλάλησεν, εἶτα ἡσύχασεν· ἠγάπησεν, εἶτα ἐμίσησε. Τὰ γὰρ ἐν ἀνθρώποις πράγματα ποτὲ μὲν πολεμεῖται, ἄλλοτε δὲ εἰρηνεύεται, ὀξυρρόπως τῶν πραγμάτων ἐξ ἀγαθῶν εἶναι δοκούντων εἰς ὁμολογούμενα κακὰ μεταπιπτόντων. Παυσώμεθα τοίνυν ἐξ ἀνονήτων μόχθων. Ταῦτα γὰρ ἅπαντα, ὥς γέ μοι δοκεῖ, κέντροις ἰοβόλοις ἀνθρώπους ἐξοιστρεῖν ἐτέθη. Καιροσκόπος δή τις πονηρὸς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦτον περικέχηνεν, ἀφανίσαι ὑπερδιατεινόμενος τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ πλάσμα, ἐξ ἀρχῆς αὐτῷ μέχρι τέλους πολεμεῖν ᾑρημένος. Πέπεισμαι τοίνυν τὰ μέγιστα ἀγαθὰ ἀνθρώπῳ εὐθυμίαν καὶ εὐποιΐαν ὑπάρχειν, καὶ μέν τοι καὶ τὴν πρόσκαιρον ταύτην ἀπόλαυσιν ἐκ Θεοῦ παραγενέσθαι μόνον, εἰ δικαιοσύνη τῶν πράξεων ἡγοῖτο. Τῶν δὲ αἰωνίων καὶ ἀφθάρτων πραγμάτων, ὅσα ὁ Θεὸς παγίως ὥρισεν, οὔτε τι ἀφελεῖν, οὔτε τι προσθεῖναι δυνατόν. ᾯ τινι οὖν, ἀλλ᾽ ἔστιν, ἐκεῖνα φοβερά τε ὁμοῦ καὶ θαυμαστά· καὶ τὰ μὲν γενόμενα, ἕστηκε· τὰ δὲ ἐσόμενα, ἤδη κατὰ τὸ προεγνῶσθαι γεγένηται. Θεῷ δὲ κέχρηται ὁ ἀδικούμενος βοηθῷ.
thought_title: Time full of opposites and the devil's war on God's creation
orientation: Solomon continues his teaching, describing how the present age is filled with contrary events and how a wicked opportunist wars against God's creation, concluding that true good is cheerfulness and beneficence from God, while eternal things fixed by God cannot be altered.
pass_a_gloss: But this time is full of all opposites: of births, then of deaths; of plants sprouting, then of their uprooting; of healings and of killings; of houses being set upright and of their dissolution; of weepings and of laughters; of mournings and of dancings. Now someone gathers the things from the earth, now he casts them out; and at one time he clings to a woman, at another he loathes her. And now someone seeks anything, now he loses it; and now he guards it, now he squanders it; at one time he killed, at another he was murdered; he spoke, then he fell silent; he loved, then he hated. For the things among humans at one time are warred over, at another they are at peace, with things turning sharply from goods that seem to be into acknowledged evils. Let us cease therefore from useless labors. For all these things, as it seems to me, were appointed to drive men mad with poisonous stings. And a certain wicked opportunist has gaped over this age, stretching himself out to destroy God's creature, having chosen from the beginning to war against it until the end. I am persuaded therefore that the greatest goods for a human being are cheerfulness and beneficence, and indeed also that this temporal enjoyment comes from God alone, if righteousness leads the actions. But of the eternal and incorruptible things, as many as God has fixed firmly, it is possible neither to take away anything nor to add anything. To whomsoever therefore, yet there is, those things are both fearful and wonderful; and the things that have happened stand fixed; and the things that will be have already come to pass according to the foreknowing. But God uses the wronged person as a helper.

lemmas.gloss: opportunist / one who watches for the right moment

choices.why: Pairs birth and death as the first opposite pair in the list, matching the order of the source.
Refers to plants being pulled up or overturned, parallel to βλαστήσεως φυτῶν.
Κόπετός denotes ritual mourning, beating the breast; paired with ὀρχημάτων (dancings).
Ἀποστυγέω means to feel disgust or loathing toward someone formerly clung to.
Προϊημί in middle voice means to let go, give up, or squander what was guarded.
One who watches for the opportune moment; here a wicked figure exploiting the age.

pass_b_english: This present time overflows with every kind of opposite: births, then deaths; the sprouting of plants, then their uprooting; healings and killings; the building up of houses and their tearing down; weeping and laughter; mournings and dancings. Now someone gathers what comes from the earth, now he casts it out. At one moment he is mad for a woman, at the next he loathes her. Now he seeks something, now he loses it; now he guards it, now he squanders it; at one time he kills, at another he is killed; he speaks, then falls silent; he loves, then hates. For human affairs are at one time at war, at another at peace, as things that seem good veer sharply into acknowledged evils. Let us therefore cease from empty and useless toils. All these things, as it seems to me, were set in place to drive people mad with poisonous goads. A wicked opportunist has gaped around this age, straining to obliterate God's creation, having chosen from the beginning to war against it until the end. I am convinced that the greatest goods for a human being are cheerfulness and doing good, and that even this fleeting enjoyment comes from God only if righteousness leads his actions. As for the eternal and imperishable things that God has fixed firmly, nothing can be taken from them and nothing can be added. For anyone, then—yet so it is—those things are at once terrifying and wonderful. The things that have happened stand fixed; the things that will be have already come to pass through God's foreknowledge. And the one who is wronged has recourse to God as helper.

problems.quote: At one moment he clings to a woman
problems.why: ἐπιμέμηνε means he has been madly enamored of a woman, not that he clings to her.
problems.fix: At one moment he is mad for a woman, at the next he loathes her.
problems.ruling: ἐπιμέμηνε γυναικί means 'is madly infatuated with a woman'; 'clings to' loses the madness/passion and is much weaker, and contrasts with ἀποστυχεῖ.

problems.quote: They are both terrifying and wonderful for whoever possesses them.
problems.source_quote: ᾯ τινι οὖν, ἀλλ᾽ ἔστιν, ἐκεῖνα φοβερά τε ὁμοῦ καὶ θαυμαστά
problems.why: The dative means for anyone, and ἀλλ᾽ ἔστιν asserts that this is so; possession is not claimed.
problems.fix: For anyone, then—yet so it is—those things are at once terrifying and wonderful.
problems.ruling: ᾯ τινι οὖν, ἀλλ᾽ ἔστιν asserts that those things exist as terrifying and wonderful; 'for whoever possesses them' invents possession and dative sense not in the Greek.

edits.old: At one moment he clings to a woman, at the next he loathes her.
edits.new: At one moment he is mad for a woman, at the next he loathes her.

edits.old: They are both terrifying and wonderful for whoever possesses them.
edits.new: For anyone, then—yet so it is—those things are at once terrifying and wonderful.

fixed: Changed 'clings to a woman' to 'is mad for a woman' to match ἐπιμέμηνε (perfect of ἐπιμάομαι: 'be madly enamored of').
Changed 'for whoever possesses them' to 'For anyone, then—yet so it is' to reflect the dative ᾧ τινι and the affirmative particle ἀλλ᾽ ἔστιν.

problems.quote: And God serves as a helper for the wronged.
problems.source_quote: Θεῷ δὲ κέχρηται ὁ ἀδικούμενος βοηθῷ.
problems.why: The wronged person is the subject who makes use of God as helper; English makes God the one who serves.
problems.fix: And the one who is wronged has recourse to God as helper.
problems.ruling: κέχρηται ὁ ἀδικούμενος βοηθῷ: the wronged man is the subject and has used God (Θεῷ) as helper. The English reverses this, making God the agent.

problems.quote: A wicked opportunist has seized hold of this age
problems.source_quote: Καιροσκόπος δή τις πονηρὸς τὸν αἰῶνα τοῦτον περικέχηνεν
problems.why: περικέχηνεν means he has gaped around this age to devour it, not that he has seized it.
problems.fix: A wicked opportunist has gaped around this age, straining to obliterate God's creation
problems.ruling: περικέχηνεν means 'gapes around' with open jaws, which is predatory lurking. 'Has seized hold of' is a different action and loses the image.

problems.quote: comes from God alone, provided that righteousness guides his actions
problems.source_quote: ἐκ Θεοῦ παραγενέσθαι μόνον, εἰ δικαιοσύνη τῶν πράξεων ἡγοῖτο
problems.why: μόνον goes with the condition: the enjoyment comes from God only if righteousness leads. 'From God alone' makes God the sole source and weakens the condition.
problems.fix: and that even this fleeting enjoyment comes from God only if righteousness leads his actions.
problems.ruling: μόνον sits before εἰ, meaning enjoyment comes from God only if δικαιοσύνη ἡγοῖτο; not “from God alone.”

edits.old: A wicked opportunist has seized hold of this age, stretching himself out to obliterate God's creation, having chosen from the beginning to war against it until the end.
edits.new: A wicked opportunist has gaped around this age, straining to obliterate God's creation, having chosen from the beginning to war against it until the end.

edits.old: I am convinced that the greatest goods for a human being are cheerfulness and doing good, and that even this fleeting enjoyment comes from God alone, provided that righteousness guides his actions.
edits.new: I am convinced that the greatest goods for a human being are cheerfulness and doing good, and that even this fleeting enjoyment comes from God only if righteousness leads his actions.

edits.old: And God serves as a helper for the wronged.
edits.new: And the one who is wronged has recourse to God as helper.

fixed: Fixed 'seized hold of this age' to 'gaped around this age, straining to obliterate...' matching περικέχηνεν (gaped around) and ὑπερδιατεινόμενος (stretching/outstretching).
Fixed 'comes from God alone, provided that...' to 'comes from God only if...' matching μόνον with the conditional εἰ clause.
Fixed 'God serves as a helper for the wronged' to 'the one who is wronged has recourse to God as helper' matching subject (ὁ ἀδικούμενος) and κέχρηται (uses/has recourse to).

last_rejected.quote: comes from God only if righteousness leads his actions
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐκ Θεοῦ παραγενέσθαι μόνον, εἰ δικαιοσύνη τῶν πράξεων ἡγοῖτο
last_rejected.why: μόνον means the enjoyment comes from God alone; English attaches “only” to the condition and makes righteousness direct “his” actions.
last_rejected.fix: and that this fleeting enjoyment comes from God alone, if the righteousness of one's deeds leads the way.
last_rejected.ruling: μόνον, ἐκ Θεοῦ παραγενέσθαι μόνον, εἰ δικαιοσύνη… ἡγοῖτο, plausibly reads as 'only if', so the English is within the range. 'His' for τῶν πράξεων is trivial.
